_comment: Pinned source of truth for every mod on the Valheim estate. The server install, Mike's client, and the published client modpack are all generated from or checked against this file. Edit it FIRST, then deploy; never the other way round.
_versions: `version` is what Thunderstore calls the release and is what the modpack pins. `plugin_name` and `plugin_version` are what BepInEx prints in LogOutput.log, which is what scripts/mods-verify.mts compares against. They differ: the loader is packaged as 5.4.2350 and logs 5.4.23.5. A null plugin_name means the entry cannot be verified from the log, and the verifier reports that rather than passing it.

modpack.name: Utgarde_Client_Pack
modpack.description: Client mods for the Utgarde Valheim server, pinned to the versions the server runs.

server.method: scripts/mods-verify.mts against the FULL boot log after the October batch (ServersideQoL, ContainerSigns and AutoProcess 2.2.0, AdventureBackpacks 2.2.5, OdinHorse 1.7.7, BuildOnShip 3.6.3, WebMap 2.1.6, Muted Mist 1.0.1, Server devcommands 1.115.0). The box downloaded each package from Thunderstore itself and every one of the 84 staged files matched a sha256 list built from the same packages off-box before anything live was touched; all 84 live hashes matched again after the copy. Replaced files kept beside the originals as .bak.20261002T011515Z, and WebMap web/ and tools/ moved aside whole. World backup world/linux/20261002T011415Z.tgz verified (BACKUP_VERIFIED) before the stop. CLEAN at 23, with "Loaded 1 patcher method from [ServersideQoL.Patchers 2.2.0.0]" and "Chainloader startup complete (22 loaded, 0 skipped, 0 failed)". The log was fetched gzipped so the 24000-byte SSM cap did not truncate it (33692 bytes). World load: Game server connected 01:16:25Z, Zonesystem Awake 01:16:26Z, DungeonDB Start 01:16:32Z.
server.errors: 0 Exception lines in the full log. The ValheimPlus line "Failed to apply `Player_UpdatePlacementGhost_Transpile`. Free placement rotation will not work." is the known BuildOnShip conflict (see that entry); the rest are the headless video and render warnings every boot prints.
server.config: Read back after the boot: [Player] restSecondsPerComfortLevel = 120 in org.bepinex.plugins.valheim_plus.cfg (backup .pre-rested.20261002T011515Z) and [User] web_edit_bases = false in com.valheimwebmap.server.cfg (backup .pre-webedit.20261002T011515Z), the key written before 2.1.6 first read the file and kept by BepInEx.
server.unverified: PortalProgression ore gating against core 2.2.0, and AutoStore 2.1.0 against it: both declare an older core and only a player carrying ore to a portal settles the first. The rested duration in game: the setting is in effect only if a player sees a longer Rested timer. Carried from earlier: OdinOnDemand players surviving a restart, and the Build On Ship client checks.
server.idle: valheim.service and valheim-idle.timer active and enabled after the restart.

client_jetragon.method: Gale Default profile read over SSH after the 1.16.0 update, then this session's LogOutput.log from the last BepInEx banner. Updating the pack in Gale left OdinOnDemand and AdventureBackpacks at their old versions, the same Gale behaviour seen on 1.14.1, so Mike updated the three changed mods one at a time rather than Update all. Afterwards each package's manifest.json read OdinOnDemand 1.3.0, AdventureBackpacks 2.1.13 and ValheimVisualEnhanced 0.5.18, with PlantEverything 1.21.2 and GentleDeath 1.0.13 unmoved. The live OdinOnDemand.dll is the local patch build 638edefa..., put there by C:\Users\mhasl\ood-patch\deploy.ps1 over stock 85be0e14.... The session log shows 'Loading [OdinOnDemand 1.3.0]', the patch's startup line, 'Moved settings from ...OdinOnDemand/config.cfg', 'Loading [Adventure Backpacks 2.1.13]' and 'Got connection' at 22:44:27 local with no refusal, which is the first client connection on 1.3.0's new network format. The migrated com.valmedia.odinondemand.cfg holds 'Muxed Native Access = true'. Four videos took the native HTTP path, VLC held its 2000 ms lead, and Mike confirmed by ear that audio sounds right. 6 '[Error' lines and 0 exceptions in the session, none from OdinOnDemand or AdventureBackpacks.
client_jetragon.stale: Pack 1.19.0 moves AdventureBackpacks to 2.2.0, which is enforced, so jetragon is refused until Gale updates it. The record above describes 1.18.0.

pack.method: scripts/modpack-publish.mts from a checkout matching main. Its post-check read 404, the same per-version lag as earlier publishes; the package index then reported 1.20.0 as latest with RandyKnapp-EquipmentAndQuickSlots-3.1.3 among its dependencies, and scripts/mods-upstream.mts reported it published. The time is Thunderstore's own date_created.
pack.window: None that kicks anyone. EquipmentAndQuickSlots is client-side and not a version gate, and the removal of ValheimPerformanceOptimizations is not one either, so a client on 1.19.0 connects normally and simply lacks the new slots until it updates.

mods.why: The BepInEx loader itself. Everything below is inert without it.
mods.upgrade_5_4_2351: Only three files differ from 5.4.2350: the two core DLLs above and the Linux doorstop library, which is now stock UnityDoorstop 4.5.0 rather than the pack's own build. The Windows winhttp.dll, doorstop_config.ini and both start scripts are byte-identical. The server preloads the doorstop library from valheim.service, so it is the file that decides whether BepInEx starts at all; the old and new builds read the same 17 DOORSTOP_* environment variables (read with strings), so the unit's existing ExecStart drives the new one unchanged. Both core DLLs still report 5.4.23.5, so the banner, and therefore plugin_version and the verifier, cannot tell 5.4.2350 from 5.4.2351. Prove the new loader by these hashes on the box and by the lines only 5.4.2351 prints: the plugin GUID after each 'Loading [...]', and the '(N loaded, N skipped, N failed)' counts on 'Chainloader startup complete'. mods-verify.test.mts pins the GUID-suffixed load line.

mods.why: Craft-from-chest, map sharing, smelter tuning, build and taming settings. The server sets enforceMod = true, so a client on any other version is kicked at connect.
mods.note: 10.2.0 is the Valheim 1.0.15 compatibility release, published 2026-09-19, the day after the game build moved. The 10.1.2 it replaces shipped 2026-09-14 and predates the patch, so the estate ran a pre-patch V+ on a post-patch server for four days. Two behaviour changes ship with it and NEITHER bites this box, both read off the regenerated config on 2026-09-22. difficultyScaleRange defaulted to 2 metres whenever the Game section was enabled, which was a bug, and now defaults to 100; here [Game] carries enabled = false, so the 200 set in that section is inert and always was. Oven settings now affect only the oven rather than every fuel-burning cooking station. The new [FrigidKiln] and [FrostFoundry] sections for the 1.0.15 Deep North stations were written into the config at lines 912 and 957, which is independent evidence the new DLL generated it rather than inheriting the old one. enforceMod = true at line 2041, so the client pack has to match this pin exactly.
mods.config_craft_from_chest: Set on the box 2026-09-26 05:30Z at the operator's request: [CraftFromChest] range 20 -> 50, allowCraftingFromCarts and allowCraftingFromShips false -> true. enabled, checkFromWorkbench (range measured from the workbench when inside its area) and ignorePrivateAreaCheck = false (wards still block other bases) unchanged. Edited while stopped, read back after the restart unchanged; [Server] serverSyncsConfig = true pushes it to clients, so no pack change. Backup beside the file as org.bepinex.plugins.valheim_plus.cfg.pre-cfc50.<stamp>. Craft From Backpack is a different mod's setting (AdventureBackpacks 2.2.0, client-local and on by default).
mods.config_rested: Set on the box 2026-10-02 at the operator's request: [Player] restSecondsPerComfortLevel 60 -> 120. [Player] was already enabled (cropNotifier lives there), and serverSyncsConfig pushes it to every player. It changes only the per-comfort-level term: on the Valheim wiki's formula of 8 minutes at comfort 1 plus one step per further level, comfort 18 goes from 25 to 42 minutes and comfort 21 from 28 to 48. The 8-minute base does not scale, so a low-comfort campfire gains little. The operator chose 120 over 150 (50 minutes at comfort 18) to keep it a little lower.
mods.config_experience: Set on the box 2026-10-04 03:33Z at the operator's request: every [Experience] skill modifier 50 -> 100, so skill gain goes from 1.5x to 2x. The section holds 23 skill keys, all of which were 50. ValheimPlus applies the modifier to RaiseSkill's factor from the server-synced config. This server has no Configuration Manager, so ValheimPlus reads the file only at launch: verified backup world/linux/20261004T033304Z.tgz, edited while stopped, read back after the restart as 23 keys at 100. Backup beside the file as org.bepinex.plugins.valheim_plus.cfg.pre-skill2x.20261004T033322Z.

mods.why: Mod library. Server-side it backs ServersideQoL; client-side it is required by Animal Feeding Trough and, since pack 1.10.0, by Muted_Mist.
mods.note: AdventureBackpacks pins this exactly, so the two move together or not at all, and the floor has now moved three times inside this estate's life: 2.26.1, then 2.30.1, now 2.30.2. The zip uses Windows path separators: unzip normalises them, a plain Python extractall does not. 2.30.2 fixes Deep North assets overriding vanilla ones and the legacy build menu breaking under 2.30.1's category changes.

mods.why: Berry bushes, thistle, dandelions, mushrooms and several trees on the cultivator. Degrades rather than blocking: a client without it still sees what others plant.
mods.upgrade_1_21_3: Compiled against Valheim 1.0.15 and BepInEx 5.4.2351, which closes this mod's gap against game_version; it declares BepInExPack 5.4.2351, which is why it moved with the loader. Also refines initialisation during config sync. The package ships the DLL as Advize_PlantEverything.dll; the key above keeps the name recorded for it earlier. It embeds ServerSync, which can refuse a client below a minimum version, but no version literal appears in the DLL's strings, so no minimum is set and a 1.21.2 client should still connect. That is read from the binary, not tested.

mods.why: ServersideQoL dependency server-side; AdventureBackpacks declares it client-side too, so every player now carries it.

Framework the three ServersideQoL modules below plug into. 2.0.4 silently stopped on the 1.0.12 network-version bump and took PortalProgression down with it, so this pin is load-bearing after every game patch.
mods.note: Ships TWO artifacts and they must move together: plugins/ServersideQoL.dll and patchers/ServersideQoL.Patchers.dll, which BepInEx loads first and which patches assembly_valheim. Upgrading only the plugin leaves the patcher a version behind, and the load log reports both, so check the 'Loaded 1 patcher method from [ServersideQoL.Patchers ...]' line as well as the plugin line. 2.0.14 turns config auto-reload on by default and fixes occasional item loss when a module modifies a container on a non-dedicated server.
mods.upgrade_2_1_0: Taken 2026-09-26 at the operator's request once moves 1 and 2 were done, after it had been held as hours old. Its own fixes are for TameAssist feeding from containers and a host-inventory bug on non-dedicated servers, neither of which this estate runs, so the reason is currency rather than a fix. Declares BepInExPack 5.4.2351 and YamlDotNet 16.3.1, both already here. Both artifacts and plugins/ServersideQoL.deps.json changed and were installed together.
mods.upgrade_2_2_0: Taken 2026-10-02 with ContainerSigns and AutoProcess 2.2.0, which both declare this core version exactly. Its own changelog line is only that the host-install warning prints once, but the release also carries a Fermenter tap RPC that AutoProcess 2.2.0 uses and an opt-out for reinitialising processors on config change (commits 8558a2b and 103569 upstream). Dependencies unchanged (BepInExPack 5.4.2351, YamlDotNet 16.3.1). PortalProgression 2.0.11 and AutoStore 2.1.0 stay on their pins because nothing newer exists; both declare an older core, and upstream does not say whether they run against 2.2.0, so the ore gate needs re-checking in game.

mods.why: Boss-gated ore through portals. The group voted for progression gating over free teleporting.
mods.note: 2.0.11 is this module's latest and it declares a hard dependency on ServersideQoL 2.0.11, while the core here runs 2.0.14. That mismatch is normal for this author, who releases the core more often than the modules, and the estate has run a newer core under a 2.0.11 module since 2026-09-18 with the load log clean. The pin is Thunderstore's resolver, not a runtime check. Verify this module by BEHAVIOUR after any core bump rather than by its load line: it is the module that logged a clean load and silently stopped gating ore on the 1.0.12 network bump, which is the incident the whole verification habit exists for.

mods.why: Auto-sort, auto-pickup, and stack-into-nearby-chests on the Cheer emote.
mods.note: 2.1.0 adds AutoPickupRangeSignPrefix (a per-chest pickup range written on its sign) and SuppressContainerModifiedEffectSound. Both are new options with defaults, so nothing here changes until someone sets them.

mods.why: Content signs on chests, and how a chest is designated for other ServersideQoL modules.
mods.note: 2.0.11 moved two settings out of this mod: AutoPickupMaxRange went to AutoStore and FeedFromContainersMaxRange went to AutoProcess, which this estate now installs. Both were sitting at the default of 64 here, so nothing needed re-homing, but a future custom value set on the wrong side of that split goes silently inert. 2.1.0 reads the new AutoStore sign prefix and fixes the range emoji on some platforms.
mods.upgrade_2_2_0: Taken 2026-10-02. Changes to the *RangeSignPrefix settings now apply without a restart. Declares ServersideQoL 2.2.0, so it moved with the core.

mods.why: Feeds smelters and kilns from nearby chests, so wood goes into a kiln and ore plus fuel into a smelter without anyone standing there. Asked for by the operator 2026-09-29. Server-only: players install nothing and nothing is version-gated.
mods.note: Declares ServersideQoL 2.1.0 only, which is the core pinned here. Read off the config the server generated on 2026-09-30, not out of the DLL. A container is a feeding source when it is within FeedFromContainersRange of the station, default 4 m, and NO sign is needed for that: any chest within 4 m of a smelter feeds it, including one used for something else. A ContainerSigns automatic sign only overrides the range per chest, by writing the FeedFromContainersRangeSignPrefix (the arrows emoji) and a number on it, capped by FeedFromContainersMaxRange (64). It only feeds while no player is within FeedFromContainersMinPlayerDistance (4 m) of the station, and it leaves FeedFromContainersLeaveAtLeastFuel and FeedFromContainersLeaveAtLeastOre (1 each) behind. CapacityMultiplier and TimePerProductMultiplier also exist and both sit at the vanilla 1; changing either is a gameplay change, not a tuning detail. The earlier wording of this note said a chest is designated by the items its sign lists; the config does not say that.
mods.unverified: The operator reported on 2026-09-30 that the automation is working in game, after testing it with real ore and wood. That report did not say which parts were exercised, and it is not a log line or a captured observation. Not separately confirmed: that the bars and charcoal a station drops were collected into a chest by AutoStore (which only picks an item up into a chest that already holds that item), and that the per-chest range override written on a sign takes effect.

operator_report.source: the operator, in the session that installed it

mods.upgrade_2_2_0: Taken 2026-10-02. Adds FeedFermenters and TapFermenters (feed a fermenter from nearby chests and tap it when ready) and FeedFromContainersLeaveAtLeastFermentable; both switches ship false and were left false, so no behaviour changed. Every existing default is unchanged. Declares ServersideQoL 2.2.0.

mods.name: Animal Feeding Trough
mods.why: Boss-free feeding for tamed animals. Clients MUST have it: the server rejects a connection with "Missing mods: Animal Feeding Trough 1.0.3", observed 2026-09-12. It is Nexus-only, so the pack cannot carry it and every player installs it by hand. Replace it with a Thunderstore equivalent when a maintained one appears; the AutoFeed family is the closest, but every candidate wants an older Jotunn or BepInEx than this estate runs.

Valheim 1.0 blocks Steam achievements for anyone running mods, so this pack is what disables them. Unshamed restores them and returns the ones already earned, granting no free unlocks. It is here because the pack causes the problem it fixes. Client-only: achievements are a Steam client concern and the server has no use for it.
mods.plugin_name_note: client-side only, so it never appears in the server's load log

mods.why: Saves the server password and adds a quick-connect button for the last server, so nobody retypes it every session. Chosen over Dedryx-QuickServerConnect because it covers both jobs in one mod: two mods hooking the same join dialog and both storing passwords is a conflict waiting to happen. Client-only and purely convenience, so dropping it breaks nothing. Published 2026-09-12 and therefore unproven here; remove it if it misbehaves.
mods.plugin_name_note: client-side only, so it never appears in the server's load log

mods.why: Craftable, wearable backpacks with tiers. Replaces ArgusMagnus-ServersideQoL_Backpack, which was server-only and therefore cheaper to deploy, but was an invisible container opened by an emote rather than an item in the world. Since the pack reaches every player anyway, the deployment saving bought nothing. Jotunn-based, so a client without it is kicked at connect exactly like ValheimPlus.
mods.note: Ships a Translations/ folder beside the DLL; 35 json files as of 2.1.13 (15 at 2.1.10, the other 20 are new languages from 2.1.11), copied on both sides. 2.1.10 hard-requires Jotunn 2.30.2, so the two can never be bumped independently: the floor was 2.26.1 at 2.0.4 and 2.30.1 at 2.0.9. Two fixes in this range earn the jump on this estate specifically. 2.1.9 fixes dedicated servers failing to load backpacks while waiting on a user-interface event, which is a server-side fault this box was exposed to. 2.1.9 also fixes cold effects bleeding through when a weather mod is running, naming Seasonality, which this estate runs with every season set to two days, so winter arrives often.
mods.telemetry: 2.0.6 added anonymous telemetry its changelog described as defaulting to enabled with auto-opt-in on launch. 2.0.9 REVERSED that, and 2.1.10 holds the line: read off the box's regenerated config on 2026-09-22, 'Enable Anonymous Telemetry' under [Local Config] is false and marked [Not Synced with Server], so the server cannot set it for players either way. That is a re-read at 2.1.10, not the 2.0.9 reading carried forward. The same section carries 'Show Splash on Startup = true', also client-local, so players see a splash on first launch after updating.
mods.upgrade_2_1_13: Dependencies are unchanged from 2.1.10 (BepInExPack 5.4.2350, Jotunn 2.30.2, YamlDotNet 16.3.1). What earns it here: 2.1.13 fixes backpacks carrying ore or metal being blocked at Stone Portals, and adds safety checks against crafting and inventory errors on dedicated servers; 2.1.11 adds more dedicated-server protections and null safety when crafting from a backpack; 2.1.12 fixes a config sync problem in a library. Enforced, so it moved with the pack.
mods.upgrade_2_2_0: Taken 2026-09-26, the same night as 2.1.13, while only jetragon had updated to the 1.18.0 pack, so no other player had to update twice. Only the DLL changed (the 35 translation files are byte-identical to 2.1.13) and the dependencies are unchanged. It adds crafting from the backpack with a consumption priority and a keep-one-of-each safeguard. It also moves Craft From Backpack, Craft Output To Backpack, Auto Store and Inventory Overflow from server-synced [Server Config] to a client-local [Automation (Local Only)] section, so the server can no longer set them for players and each player's own config decides. This server never set them (defaults applied), so the move changes nothing here unless a player's local defaults differ.
mods.upgrade_2_2_5: Taken 2026-10-02 in pack 1.21.0. Dependencies unchanged. A BALANCE CHANGE ships with it: 2.2.4 makes every backpack give armor, 1 per backpack level by default, and adds a choice of whether the speed penalty shrinks with upgrades. Left at defaults. Fixes in range that matter here: 2.2.2 stops ore inside a backpack bypassing portal restrictions in rare cases, 2.2.3 stops a death or tombstone pickup scattering a backpack's contents on the ground, and 2.2.4 hardens dedicated-server startup.

mods.why: Dedicated slots for worn gear (head, chest, legs, shoulder, utility, trinket) plus up to six hotkeyable quick slots. Picked by the operator 2026-09-29 over shudnal-ExtraSlots, which adds food, ammo and misc slots with progression gating and an AdventureBackpacks integration; the simpler mod won. Declares BepInExPack 5.4.2201 and Jotunn 2.29.2, both under the versions already here.
mods.plugin_name_note: client-side only, so it never appears in the server's load log
mods.note: Its readme says it is client-installable and not needed on the server; a server copy would sync the balance settings (slot toggles, quick slot count, keep-on-death) and admin-control them. Not installed on the server, so each player's own config decides, and Utility Slot Count defaults to 1 and is off by default. It declares ExtraSlots, ComfyQuickSlots, AzuExtendedPlayerInventory and ExtendedPlayerInventory incompatible, so BepInEx refuses to load it beside any of them; none is pinned here. Per its changelog, 3.0.0 migrates a character's items into the new slots on first login with NO downgrade path, so removing the mod later needs the slots cleared first. Its 3.0.1 notes cover ValheimPlus with the [Inventory] section enabled.
mods.unverified: Not tested against Vapok-AdventureBackpacks 2.2.0 here; ExtraSlots documents an AdventureBackpacks integration and this mod's readme does not mention it. Its declared game target was not read. Watch the first login of the first player who updates: an item that is missing afterwards is what eaqs_restorebackup is for.

mods.why: Keeps equipables (weapons, armor, tools, shields, ammo, utility, trinkets) on death and sends everything else to the tombstone, classifying via Valheim's own ItemData.IsEquipable(). Replaces beefbaccio-DeathTweaks, which shipped in pack 1.3.0 and coincided with every player stuck at 1 health; that attribution was never proven, but DeathTweaks predated Valheim 1.0 and this one declares 1.0.x compatibility. Verified working on jetragon 2026-09-15.
mods.plugin_name_note: client-side only, so it never appears in the server's load log
mods.note: 1.0.14 only moves its declared dependency to BepInExPack 5.4.2351, per the author's changelog. Taken with the loader so the pin stays current, not for any behaviour.

mods.why: Scales swim speed, stamina regen and stamina drain to the Swim skill, and adds diving. Vanilla swimming was the complaint. Verified on jetragon 2026-09-15.
mods.plugin_name_note: client-side only, so it never appears in the server's load log

mods.why: Ground transport: a tameable, rideable, breedable horse with armour and an attachable cart. Added 2026-09-18 because overland travel to the traders and back is the group's standing complaint, and vanilla offers nothing below the Plains lox saddle. Chosen on maintenance rather than features: it is the only mod in this category still shipping, updated 2026-09-15, against a field where the nearest alternatives (BeastsOfBurden 2021, CraftyCartsRemake and ValheimRAFT early 2026) are stale. Declares no dependencies and bundles its assets in a 10.5 MB DLL, so it needs nothing else on the box. Config syncs from the server like ValheimPlus.
mods.note: It DOES enforce an exact version, despite not being Jotunn-based: on 2026-10-02 the operator joined the 1.7.7 server with 1.7.3 still in Gale and was refused with a message that the client had 1.7.3 and needed 1.7.7. So every OdinHorse bump is a two-sided change with a kick window, like AdventureBackpacks. Whether it rejects a client that lacks it entirely is still untested. Its own readme opens by telling you to back up character and world files before installing or updating. 1.7.1 through 1.7.3 are a piecemanager bump and added localisations, with no behaviour change the changelog names.
mods.upgrade_1_7_7: Taken 2026-10-02 in pack 1.21.0, the day 1.7.7 was published. Player-visible changes: the Wait Here key moves from T to Y (1.7.4), horses jump on Jump while riding and Use dismounts (1.7.6), and mounted combat arrives (1.7.5), on by default only for NEW configs (1.7.6, 1.7.7), so this server's existing Raelaziel.OdinHorse.cfg keeps whatever it had. The readme says all players need the mod for mounted combat. OdinHorse 1.7.8 was published at 01:16Z during this deploy (Cart Width/Height settings, a fix for error spam when a ridden horse dies, dual-wield animation compatibility) and is NOT taken yet.

mods.why: Build on the vanilla Karve and Longship: walls, crafting stations, chests, beds that set a respawn point, and portals that travel with the ship. Picked on 2026-09-23 over zolantris-ValheimRAFT 5.0.4 because the operator wanted to use the existing ships rather than build custom ones from pieces. Known conflict: ValheimPlus says its free placement rotation (LeftAlt, C and V while placing a piece) will not work with this mod installed, because both mods rewrite the same placement code. It is in the pack on trial anyway. If losing free rotation costs you more than building on ships gives you, tell the operator and it can come out.
mods.risk: MAINTENANCE risk only. Every version on Thunderstore is dated 2026-09-16 to 2026-09-21, and recent changelog entries fix "disappearing structures" and "duplicate portals on ships", so the mod is young and still settling. On the fourth drift the readme declares only "Valheim 0.219+", a floor rather than a tested build, so the check against game_version 1.0.15 is INDETERMINATE. Sole declared dependency is BepInExPack 5.4.2333, older than the 5.4.2350 here.
mods.conflict: ValheimPlus free placement rotation is lost while this mod is installed, which is why the why above warns players. The pinned DLL patches Player.UpdatePlacementGhost, including a transpiler (ShipBuildingMod.Player_Patches.UpdatePlacementGhost_Transpiler), and that is the method ValheimPlus's Player_UpdatePlacementGhost_Transpile rewrites. BepInEx breaks load-order ties by GUID, so ShipBuildMod (com.custom.shipbuildmod) loads ahead of ValheimPlus (org.bepinex.plugins.valheim_plus), at server log lines 23 and 48, and ValheimPlus then fails to find the code it expects. Proven on the server by a before and after: the first boot with Build On Ship, 2026-09-25 05:37Z, logged 'Failed to apply `Player_UpdatePlacementGhost_Transpile`. Free placement rotation will not work.' twice, while the journal shows that line on no earlier boot back to 2026-09-10. That includes all 71 boots since a config snapshot first shows [FreePlacementRotation] enabled (2026-09-12 01:58Z), the last of them at 00:03Z the same day with every mod but this one. The loss is real, not cosmetic: enabled = true in the server's ValheimPlus config (read 2026-09-25), and serverSyncsConfig pushes it to clients. A client logging the same line is expected, because the pack loads the same two mods in the same GUID order, but it is UNVERIFIED; the first player to press LeftAlt while placing a piece settles it. Shipped anyway on the operator's call, 2026-09-25: 'Ship both anyway', then 'if it breaks we can always remove it'. Removing this mod restores rotation but may strand pieces built on ships (see note), so take a world backup first.
mods.note: The DLL's BepInPlugin attribute is com.custom.shipbuildmod, ShipBuildMod, 4.0.0, so the log shows 4.0.0 against Thunderstore's 3.4.3. Read off the DLL, then confirmed on the first server boot with it (2026-09-25 05:37Z), which logged 'Loading [ShipBuildMod 4.0.0]' and the mod's own 'ShipBuildMod v4.0.0 loaded successfully.' It declares no BepInProcess restriction, so it loads under the dedicated server. It carries no ServerSync and no Jotunn NetworkCompatibility, so nothing refuses a client that lacks it; what such a client sees on a built-on ship is UNVERIFIED. The ship link is stored in ZDO fields (ShipBuild_ParentUUID, ShipBuild_ShipUUID, ShipBuild_LocalPos, ShipBuild_LocalRot), so assume removing the mod strands built pieces and take a world backup before uninstalling. Ship portals are ordinary portal pieces, so PortalProgression's ore gate should apply to them unchanged; UNVERIFIED.
mods.upgrade_3_6_3: Taken 2026-10-02 in pack 1.21.0. The changelog is thin: 3.5.0 says 'Fix 20.09.26. Ship control', 3.6.0 has no entry, and 3.6.1 to 3.6.3 each say 'nothing'. The DLL still declares ShipBuildMod 4.0.0, so the log line does not move. The free placement rotation conflict above is not mentioned upstream and is assumed to persist.

mods.why: Seasonal textures and colours, plus weather. Chosen over shudnal-Seasons because that one carries gameplay effects on crops and water, and we had just finished tuning crop growth. Modifiers Enabled ships Off and every per-season stat multiplier is 1, so out of the box it is purely visual, which is what was asked for. Depends on YamlDotNet, already carried for AdventureBackpacks.
mods.why_server_side: Client-only was tried first, on the reasoning that the season derives from world age so clients would agree without server sync. Measured 2026-09-18: seasons never advanced, sitting on the configured Summer for days while the client logged a healthy load. Installed server-side the same night, after which the server logs 'Seasonal Timer Awake'. The mod's README lists season_winter and siblings as GLOBAL KEYS, which only a server writes, and every config entry is marked [Synced with Server] with the in-game set command admin-only. Those point the same way but do not by themselves prove the old reasoning wrong; the proof is a season actually flipping, which had not yet happened when this was written.
mods.note: Ships a config/Seasonality texture tree alongside the DLL; a mod manager places it, a hand install must copy it into BepInEx/config. Season lengths live in the server's copy of the config as a Vector3 of days, hours, minutes, with 30 real minutes to the in-game day. All four are set to two days, against a stock default of five in-game hours that cycles a whole year every 25 real minutes. 3.8.3 adds a Warm_Twilight_SnowStorm environment because vanilla's Twilight_SnowStorm became freezing in Valheim 1.0, and instructs you to reset configs or change winter weather by hand. Checked against this estate's config on 2026-09-18 and it does NOT apply: Twilight_SnowStorm appears nowhere here, every [Winter] weather list already reads WarmSnow:1,Twilight_Snow:0.5,WarmSnowStorm:0.1, and Always Cold and Wet Freezes are both Off. Re-check that grep rather than the changelog if the warning resurfaces.

mods.why: Browser map of the live world, served from the box over the Cloudflare tunnel, showing the terrain every player has explored plus player pins and pin sharing. Server-side only: it renders from the world the server holds, so clients install nothing. Chosen over Mubs-WebMap and the other h0tw1r3 forks because it is the one still shipping, and because it keeps the 3D view and renders history rather than only what is explored while it runs.
mods.note: Ships a web/ tree beside the DLL and writes rendered tiles into plugins/WebMap/map_data, which reached 110 MB on first full reveal, so it is not a candidate for the backup set. Its zip uses Windows path separators, so a plain extractall produces files literally named 'plugins\WebMap\web\js\app.js'; normalise the separators on extract. The three h0tw1r3 forks share the config filename com.github.h0tw1r3.valheim.webmap.cfg, so a fork swap that leaves the old file behind silently inherits the previous fork's values.
mods.upgrade_2_1_6: Taken 2026-10-02. Adds renaming and hiding auto-detected bases from the web page, 3D view links, sharper 2D close-ups, and base_min_pieces / base_min_per_cell. The base editing is open to anyone who can load the map unless [User] web_edit_bases = false, and the map is served publicly over the tunnel, so web_edit_bases was set false on the box before the first 2.1.6 boot; the token holder can still edit. The web/ tree was replaced with the release's copy and map_data was left alone.

mods.why: The visual upgrade the group asked for. Explicitly NOT a ReShade-style screen filter: its effects hook Valheim's own lighting, water, weather, biome and time-of-day systems, so they respond to the world rather than tinting the frame. Ships wind-driven cloud shadows, underwater caustics and Meadows fireflies on by default. Chosen over the texture-replacement mods because those are limited to vegetation and their own author recommends this one instead.
mods.plugin_name_note: client-side only, so it never appears in the server's load log
mods.note: Requires Direct3D 11; its readme states Vulkan is not currently validated, so a client launching with -force-vulkan may misbehave. Windows only. Declares no Jotunn dependency and no network sync. More usefully than that reasoning, it was OBSERVED on 2026-09-19 that a client lacking this batch's mods connected and spawned normally (05:40:44Z), and neither new server-side DLL carries a Jotunn NetworkCompatibility string, so nothing here enforces a version match. Its own readme says do NOT install it on a dedicated server; it has no server-side behaviour. The Enhanced Environment colour-grading feature ships Enabled = false and was deliberately left off: it is the one opinionated feature and visibly recolours the game. 0.5.15 through 0.5.17 tune the three features that ship on by default: cloud shadows now form in broad bands rather than one uniform dapple size, the finest shadow octave is dropped when the mask cannot resolve it, which removes shimmer at high ShadowDrawDistance, and underwater caustics now fall off on vertical faces instead of lighting walls like floors. Its zip uses Windows path separators, the same trap as Jotunn's. 0.5.18 only raises the default Water Caustic Lighting intensity to 1.8; a client with an existing config keeps its saved value, so for current players it changes nothing.

mods.why: Grass density and draw distance, so clutter stops popping in a few metres ahead of the player. Chosen on currency rather than popularity: ShadowField-GrassTweaks has ten times the downloads and is recommended by other mods' readmes, but was last updated 2025-07-26, before Valheim 1.0. This one was updated 2026-09-14 and declares no dependencies at all. Its own readme nonetheless says 'Built for Valheim 1.0.12', three patches behind this estate's 1.0.15, which is a real qualification on the currency argument above: recent upload date and declared target build are different things, and none of the three drift checks compares the latter against game_version.
mods.plugin_name_note: client-side only, so it never appears in the server's load log
mods.upgrade_0_2_301: Taken 2026-10-02 in pack 1.21.0. The author's whole changelog for it: 'the old 0.2.3 was actually 0.2.2 and i uploaded the wrong dll 2 weeks ago' and '0.2.301 is Quite literally just the real 0.2.3'. So the 0.2.3 pinned here was the 0.2.2 build all along. What 0.2.3 changes over 0.2.2 is not stated. The readme still says 'Built for Valheim 1.0.12', against game_version 1.0.16.

mods.why: Draw distance: controls how far zones are rendered, loaded and generated. Its readme says to install it on the server and optionally on clients, so the server copy is what the client's own limits are raised against; whether extended limits are strictly impossible without it is untested here. This is a maintained fork of JereKuusela's Render Limits, rebuilt and smoke-tested against Valheim 1.0.14 at network version 40. The network version matches this estate; the game version does not, since this estate runs 1.0.15. and it preserves the original render_limits plugin GUID and config keys.
mods.note: Installed at stock values. 1.16.0 specifically added server-side guardrails against a client requesting an excessive loaded radius, plus a 'Maximum force active zones' bound, so raising limits is a deliberate follow-up rather than something to crank blind. Each zone is 64x64 m.

mods.why: Thins the Mistlands mist instead of deleting it. One setting, TransparencyIntensity, where 0 hides the mist entirely and 1 is vanilla. The estate ran 0.7, a gentle trim, through the Mistlands, and was set to 0 when the group beat the Queen (operator, 2026-10-04): the mist was the price of the biome, and it was paid. That 0 did not clear the mist in game; see `server_value_does_not_redraw`. Chosen over Vapok-NoFogBruh, which removes fog outright and was rejected as effectively cheating in the Mistlands, and over ComfyMods-Dramamist, which does the same job but predates Valheim 1.0.
mods.note: Config changes take effect LIVE, with no restart, which is unusual on this estate and makes it the cheapest setting here to tune in place. Installed server-side deliberately: its readme says a server install enforces the configuration on clients, and leaving it off the server would let each player choose, but it is the only mod in this batch that declares a Jotunn dependency, which is the one kick path this estate has actually seen fire. That made it the likeliest to enforce a version match, not the only thing that conceivably could; it was afterwards observed not to enforce one. One shared value is the cheaper trade. Its shipped default is TransparencyIntensity = 0.2, which is near-invisible mist, NOT vanilla; 0.7 here is therefore a raise off the default rather than a cut from vanilla. Read the generated config before assuming a mod's default is the vanilla behaviour.
mods.upgrade_1_0_1: Taken 2026-10-02 in pack 1.21.0. Its one change lets a client change 'admin' settings locally when the SERVER lacks the mod; this server has it, so enforcement is unchanged. Dependencies move to BepInExPack 5.4.2351 and Jotunn 2.30.2, both already here. Its only declared game target is 1.0.0's 'Release for game version 1.0.7'.
mods.config_state: Set live on the box 2026-10-04T02:44:05Z with two players online: TransparencyIntensity 0.7 to 0 in /home/steam/valheim/BepInEx/config/com.orianaventure.mod.MutedMist.cfg, previous file kept as .pre-nomist.20261004T024405Z. The server log printed 'MutedMist: Attempting to reload configuration...' at the same second, with no restart. Clients receive the value through server sync, so the client pack does not change.
mods.server_value_does_not_redraw: FOUND 2026-10-04: setting 0 did NOT clear the mist in game, and neither did also setting the client's own file to 0. The 'live' claim in `note` holds only for the CLIENT's local file. Plugin.cs repaints the mist in two places, ParticleMist.Awake and a FileSystemWatcher on the local cfg that calls Config.Reload(), and nothing repaints when a server-synced value arrives; the reload re-reads the local file, so a sync that touches it repaints with the client's own value. jetragon logged that reload at 22:44:08 local while its file still held 0.2. After its file was set to 0 at 23:04 and the reload logged again, the operator still saw the mist, so the mod's single material alpha on ParticleMist.instance is not the whole Mistlands mist on this build. Treat the mod as not working until a relog test says otherwise; the operator is trying Nexus 3145 (SKK Mist remover) client-side.

mods.why: Replants a sapling where a felled tree's stump is destroyed, so logging does not permanently strip the map. Requested by the operator 2026-09-19; no reason beyond the request was given. Chosen as the only maintained member of its family: it is a rebuild of Aedenthorn's TreeRespawn, and of the surviving forks of that original the freshest is Lyric-TreeRespawn_by_Aedenthorn 0.8.5, last updated 2026-03-10, with most of the rest deprecated, against this one's 2026-09-11. Its readme declares the target as "Updated for Valheim 1.0" with no patch number, so the fourth drift check is INDETERMINATE here rather than clean: unlike WiresGrassTweaks there is no number to compare against game_version 1.0.15. Sole declared dependency is BepInExPack 5.4.2202, older than the 5.4.2350 this estate runs.
mods.note: Ships a plugins/configs/ tree beside the DLL, so a hand install must copy the folder and not just the DLL; same trap as Seasonality's config tree and AdventureBackpacks' Translations folder. ALL FOUR dictionaries must be present, because the mod picks one at RUNTIME by probing BepInEx for a planting mod's GUID: advize.PlantEverything selects tree_dict_Plant_Everything.json, com.Defryder.Plant_all_trees selects tree_dict_Plant_all_trees.json, com.bkeyes93.PlantingPlus selects tree_dict_PlantingPlus.json, and tree_dict.json is the fallback when none is loaded. This estate runs Advize-PlantEverything, so it resolves to the PlantEverything dictionary with no configuration, and that dictionary differs: it maps SwampTree1_Stub to Ancient_Sapling where the fallback maps SwampTree1 to SwampTree1. Shipping only tree_dict.json would leave the selected file missing, which is a silent failure. The mod prints "Loaded <n> seeds from <file>" on startup, so the chosen dictionary is verifiable from the server log rather than inferred. Config keys live under [General]: Enabled, RespawnDelay, treeRate, useRandomSapling, checkcraftingtable, noswamptreerespawn, GrowthSpaceRestriction, DebugMode.
mods.sync: Bundles ServerSync inside the DLL rather than declaring it as a dependency, so the server holds the config and locks it to clients. The DLL's own text says "It's required that the mod is installed on the server and all clients" and carries ServerSync's version-mismatch path ("Received server version is not equal"), so treat this as a mod that can refuse a mismatched client and keep the deploy-to-publish window short. ServerSync is not Jotunn's ModCompatibility, and whether a client lacking the mod is actually refused here is UNVERIFIED; the author's statement and the version check are the evidence, not an observation.

mods.why: Buildable shrines, one per defeated Forsaken, that channel that boss's guardian power once its trophy is mounted, so swapping a power costs a build instead of a run to the world-centre stones. Picked by the operator 2026-09-19 over turbero-ForsakenPowersPlusRemastered 2.0.4, which does the same job with an F8 hotkey. THE DECIDING AXIS WAS DESIGN, NOT PACKAGE HEALTH: a hotkey deletes the trip, while a shrine keeps the mechanic and puts a price on it, one build plus consumed trophies per boss. That is the same rule that put ServersideQoL_PortalProgression here instead of free portals, Muted_Mist instead of NoFogBruh, and GentleDeath instead of DeathTweaks: gate the mechanic, do not remove it. Depends on Jotunn 2.30.0, under the 2.30.1 already here, and on BepInExPack 5.4.2350, which matches exactly.
mods.risk: MAINTENANCE risk only, which is a separate axis from the design choice in `why` and does not qualify it. The author labels 0.8.3 ALPHA in his own readme, and it had 257 downloads at install time against the alternative's 3448, so upstream may move or stall under us. On the fourth drift it is the WIDEST gap recorded here: the readme says "Built against Valheim 1.0.7" against game_version 1.0.15, eight patches, where Wire-WiresGrassTweaks' 1.0.12 was three. None of the three drift checks can see any of that, so re-read the readme's declared target on every upgrade. The package also carries Thunderstore's AI Generated tag; recorded as a fact about the listing, explicitly NOT as a concern, because the operator has ruled that out of scope for this estate.
mods.note: UNINSTALLING THIS SERVER-SIDE PERMANENTLY DESTROYS EVERY SHRINE PLAYERS HAVE BUILT. The shrines are new prefabs, and Valheim deletes ZDOs it cannot instantiate, silently and with no recovery. That is not a hypothetical: the mod's own 0.8.3 changelog is describing what already happened to its users, because 0.8.2 and earlier carried [BepInProcess("valheim.exe")], which makes BepInEx skip the plugin entirely under valheim_server.exe, so it could not load on a dedicated server at all. Treat removal as a destructive operation needing a world backup, never as a rollback. The same reasoning is why it is side 'both' rather than client-only. Version enforcement is ServerSync's, not Jotunn's ModCompatibility: the DLL declares no NetworkCompatibility attribute, and the disconnect path it does carry refuses a client whose ForsakenShrines version differs from the server's, while a client with the mod absent entirely can still connect. So the pack and the box must move together, but a player who never installs it is not locked out. Placement is constrained: natural terrain only, open sky above, and a Stonecutter in range; shrines sit in the vanilla stone hammer tab because Valheim 1.0 hard-limits build categories. Every setting except 'Mod Enabled' is server-synced; that one is client-local and needs a relaunch. 0.8.5 fixes one arm of that destruction: setting 'Mod Enabled = false' on a dedicated server used to skip prefab registration, so the server deleted every shrine ZDO it could not resolve. A dedicated server now ignores that setting, loads anyway, and logs why. The guidance above is unchanged and is now what upstream says too: take the mod off a server by removing the DLL, never by flipping the setting. 0.8.4 added a 'Lock Configuration' setting under General, on by default and held by the server.
mods.symptom_to_remember: Spinning camera plus a character frozen in the wake-up pose on login, on Valheim 1.0, means SOME installed mod is registering build pieces through Jotunn's PieceManager, whose patch targets a field Valheim 1.0 removed; it throws every physics tick and aborts player spawning whenever a Hammer is equipped. It is not specific to this mod. ForsakenShrines 0.8.1 did it, 0.8.2 stopped using PieceManager, and Jotunn 2.30.0 fixes it for mods that still do. Worth knowing before that symptom gets chased as a graphics or client problem.
mods.config_state: Read on the box 2026-09-22 after the 0.8.5 install: 'Mod Enabled = true' and the new 'Lock Configuration = true' that 0.8.4 added, which is its shipped default and holds the synced config against client edits.

mods.why: Newtonsoft.Json, packaged for Valheim by the ValheimModding team. Carried only because OdinOnDemand declares it. Nothing else on the estate asks for it.
mods.note: The shim logs 'Newtonsoft.Json Detector 1.0.0' while the package is versioned 13.0.4, the same split the YamlDotNet shim has. Read off the box 2026-09-22 after a guess of 'Newtonsoft Json Detector' was wrong by one dot. Worth knowing: on this server it does not load anything. Its own line reads 'Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.0.0 assembly already loaded from valheim_server_Data/Managed/Newtonsoft.Json.dll', because the game itself ships Newtonsoft at that path. Detecting that and standing down is the shim's whole job, so it is doing it. The package is carried because OdinOnDemand declares it, not because the server needs it.

mods.why: OdinOnDemand's support libraries, declared as a hard dependency. Seven managed DLLs that resolve media URLs: YoutubeExplode, YoutubeDLSharp, SoundCloudExplode and four System/Bcl shims. No native code, so it is platform-neutral and safe on the Linux box.
mods.plugin_name_note: Seven plain assemblies and no BepInEx plugin, so it cannot appear in a load log on either side. Verified by file presence instead: the deploy hash-checks YoutubeExplode.dll, YoutubeDLSharp.dll and SoundCloudExplode.dll against this entry before installing, and confirms 3/3 on the box afterwards. Do not reach for the transitive argument that OdinOnDemand loading proves these are present: OdinOnDemand may only touch them on a playback path a dedicated server never takes, so its load line says nothing about them.

mods.why: Cinema screens, televisions and music players built in world, playing YouTube, SoundCloud, Twitch, Kick and direct HTTP(S) streams for everyone in earshot. Asked for by the operator 2026-09-22. 1.2 rebuilt it on LibVLC and restored its own build-menu category on Valheim 1.0's new system.
mods.enforcement: Jotunn NetworkCompatibility, confirmed by reading the strings in OdinOnDemand.dll rather than inferred from it being Jotunn-based: the assembly carries both NetworkCompatibilityAttribute and VersionStrictness. That is the same kick path that already fires for AdventureBackpacks, so the box and the published pack must move together and a player on the old pack is refused at connect.
mods.why_linux_is_fine: The package is 24.8 MB and most of it is a win-x64 LibVLC runtime, which cannot execute on this Linux box. It still loads, for reasons that were CHECKED rather than assumed. The assembly carries no BepInProcess attribute and names neither valheim.exe nor valheim_server.exe, so BepInEx does not skip it under valheim_server.exe; that is the exact way ForsakenShrines 0.8.2 failed here, so it was the first thing looked for. It does carry IsDedicated, IsServer and ZNet, so a server branch exists in the code. The readme scopes the VLC runtime to 'every client' and describes the server's job as simulating station playback position and sending it to players, which is bookkeeping rather than decoding. The libvlc tree is installed on the server anyway, inert, because the readme also says clients and servers must have identical files and 40 MB of dormant Windows DLLs is the cheaper risk.
mods.linux_boot_evidence: First server boot with it, 2026-09-22 05:55Z. The win-x64 LibVLC runtime was the open question and it is answered: 48 files and 31 MB of Windows natives sit in plugins/libvlc on a Linux box and nothing tried to touch them. A whole-word grep for vlc, libvlc and LibVLCSharp across the boot returns NOTHING, so no VLC initialisation was attempted and none failed. OdinOnDemand's own logger printed one line, its load line, which on its own would be weak evidence. The stronger evidence is that it created BepInEx/config/OdinOnDemand/ at 05:55 holding four files, including recipes.json and recipes_item.json: a mod that has written out the recipes for its own buildable pieces has run well past construction. Contrast ForsakenShrines in the same boot, which narrates every prefab it clones; OdinOnDemand is simply a quiet mod.

player_setup.summary: Screens, televisions and radios play direct audio and video links, internet radio and SoundCloud with nothing extra installed: the mod bundles its own VLC. Two sources need a free program on your own machine.

extras.install: A JavaScript runtime on your PATH. Deno 2.3 or newer is the one the mod's authors name, and it also accepts Node, Bun or QuickJS if you already have one. If you play through Proton or on a Steam Deck, use the Windows x64 `deno.exe` instead of the native Linux build.
extras.verify: The cog menu on any media player has an External JS line naming the runtime it found.
extras.without_it: YouTube still plays. The mod's authors warn that quality or audio availability may be limited, so this is the one worth doing.

extras.install: Streamlink, on your PATH, in the Valheim folder, or beside `OdinOnDemand.dll`. Under Proton use either the Windows build in one of those places, or the Linux build in `/usr/bin`, `/usr/local/bin` or `~/.local/bin`, outside the Steam runtime container.
extras.verify: The same cog menu shows whether Streamlink was detected; reopen it to re-probe after installing.
extras.without_it: Twitch and Kick links do not play. Nothing else changes, and most people will never want this one.

mods.drift_target_build: INDETERMINATE by the readme, which still says only 'Valheim 1.0 support' with no patch number. 1.3.0 was published 2026-09-25, a week after the game moved to 1.0.15 on 2026-09-18, so the concern that this mod's latest release predated the current game build no longer applies.
mods.note: The two player extras are per-player hand installs like Animal Feeding Trough, because a Thunderstore pack carries mods and nothing else. Neither is a version gate, so a player without them is not kicked, only short a source. Read off the 1.2.5 readme and re-read 2026-09-22 before any of it went on the pack page; the mod reports detection status for both in its own cog menu, which is why the page tells players to look there rather than to assume the copy took. Config lives in BepInEx/config/OdinOnDemand/ rather than a single cfg file. The readme lists admin-only settings, a VIP mode and remote-control options, none of which are configured yet.
mods.upgrade_1_3_0: Taken 2026-09-25 because its changelog calls it an 'Important security update' that servers and all players should take, without saying what the issue is. 1.3.0 changes the network message format and 'can't connect to older versions', so the box and the pack moved together. Only OdinOnDemand.dll differs from 1.2.5: every LibVLCSharp and libvlc file in the package is byte-identical, and the three declared dependencies (Jotunn 2.30.2, OOD_LIB 1.2.0, JsonDotNET 13.0.4) are unchanged. It also stops a dedicated server from trying to play media, which is the path the Linux box never exercised anyway. Settings have lived in BepInEx/config/com.valmedia.odinondemand.cfg since 1.2.6; the plugin moves an existing OdinOnDemand/config.cfg there whole on first launch, before it binds its settings.
mods.client_local_patch: jetragon does not run the stock client DLL. It runs 1.3.0 plus a local patch that sends single-file YouTube formats (format 18) through LibVLC's native HTTP access with 2000 ms of caching, which fixed a stutter where about three quarters of the audio was dropped. Source: ~/Developer/OdinOnDemand, branch local/muxed-native-access-1.3.0, commit ac89733, a port of the 1.2.5 patch 4230911, pushed nowhere. It is off unless '[YouTube] Muxed Native Access = true' is set. The patch is client-side only and does not touch networking, so it does not affect the version check. Any reinstall of OdinOnDemand through Gale restores the stock DLL silently.

mods.why: Admin console tooling: enables devcommands and the admin utilities around them on a dedicated server, which vanilla refuses to a remote admin. Installed on the box by hand on 2026-09-20 at 19:45 UTC and found by scripts/mods-verify.mts on 2026-09-22, which reported it UNEXPECTED because no record mentioned it.
mods.why_not_in_pack: Operator tooling, like the ConfigurationManager entry below. It grants console powers that are admin-gated anyway, so shipping it to five players installs something none of them can use. Recorded here rather than left out, because an absent entry reads as an oversight and the verifier will flag it as drift on every run until it is written down.
mods.note: 1.114 adds an alternative biome to minimap texts and stops the bind system running invalid or missing commands. It declares BepInExPack 5.4.2351, so it moved with the loader. It lives in its own plugins/JereKuusela-Server_devcommands/ directory rather than loose in plugins/, which is why a directory listing alone does not make it obvious.
mods.upgrade_1_115_0: Taken 2026-10-02. Adds a setting to disable the help command and fixes the alternative biome text using the wrong coordinate.

mods.why: In-game editor for every BepInEx setting, opened with F1. It is how the admin changes a [Synced with Server] value without a config edit and a server restart, which is the difference between turning the rain off in ten seconds and bouncing everyone. Added 2026-09-20, when Seasonality's weather lists needed changing mid-session and there was no way to do it from inside the game.
mods.why_not_in_pack: Operator tooling, not something the group plays with. It edits settings that are admin-only to change anyway, so shipping it to every player installs a GUI five people cannot use to change anything. Kept in this manifest rather than left out, because an absent entry reads as an oversight and invites the next session to add it to the pack; admin_only is the recorded decision not to.

game_version_note: Moved from 1.0.15 at 2026-09-25 19:10:58Z (appmanifest LastUpdated, buildid 25527701), pulled in by the SteamCMD validate that runs before every server start. Nobody noticed until BepInExPack 5.4.2351's 'Valheim Version:' line printed it at 04:25Z on 2026-09-26; the journal's own 'Valheim version: l-1.0.16 (network version 40)' line confirms it on the 02:41Z boot too. The network version stayed at 40, so clients on 1.0.16 connect ('Network version check, their:40, mine:40'). Mods whose readmes declare 1.0.15 are now one patch behind on the fourth drift.
